**VitaGen Pharmaceuticals - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript**

**Operator:**
Good morning, and welcome to the VitaGen Pharmaceuticals Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during listen-only portions of the call. To ask a question during the Q&A, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. As a further reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

**Jordan Lee, Vice President of Investor Relations:**
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss VitaGen Pharmaceuticals' financial results for the Q2 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Rachel Kim, Chief Medical Officer; and Dr. Peter Voss, Chief Scientific Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds, CEO of VitaGen Pharmaceuticals.

**Dr. Michael Reynolds, CEO:**
Thank you, Jordan. Good morning, everyone. VitaGen Pharmaceuticals delivered a strong performance in the Q2, driven by explosive new product launches, market share gains, and robust execution across our oncology and rare disease franchises. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives, focusing on new product launch updates and market share gains with OncoLink-450 and HemaGene-12 leading the charge; marketing and sales effectiveness metrics highlighting our sales force productivity and omnichannel ROI; revenue guidance and key upcoming catalysts that position us for multi-year growth; product revenue by key drug franchise including volume and price dynamics; and key assumptions and risk factors underpinning our outlook.

We are particularly excited about OncoLink-450 and its potential to capture dominant share in HER2-low metastatic breast cancer through superior efficacy and favorable safety.

Now, I will turn the call over to Maria Gonzalez, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

**Maria Gonzalez, CFO:**
Thank you, Michael, and good morning, everyone. I'm thrilled to dive into our new product launches and the impressive market share gains we're seeing across our portfolio. As you know, fiscal Q2 marked the commercial inflection point for two key launches: OncoLink-450, our next-generation antibody-drug conjugate—or ADC—targeting HER2-low metastatic breast cancer, and HemaGene-12, our AAV-based gene therapy for severe hemophilia A. These launches are executing at or above our expectations, driven by robust clinical differentiation, strategic pricing, and aggressive market access strategies. Let me break this down with the latest IQVIA and internal data.

Starting with OncoLink-450. We launched in the U.S. in late Q1 following full FDA approval on the strength of our pivotal Phase III ONCO-301 trial, which demonstrated a 28% improvement in progression-free survival—median PFS of 14.2 months versus 10.9 months for the active control—and a manageable safety profile with lower rates of interstitial lung disease at 3.2% compared to 7.1% for Enhertu, the current category leader from Daiichi Sankyo and AstraZeneca. Globally, we've secured approvals in the EU via EMA in early Q2 and in Japan through our PMDA filing, with pricing negotiations underway.

Commercial uptake has been explosive. In the U.S., Q2 net sales hit $285 million, smashing our guidance of $200-250 million and representing 420% growth quarter-over-quarter from Q1's ramp-up phase. This was fueled by NRx share among new HER2-low patients reaching 22% by week 20 post-launch, per IQVIA NPA data—up from 8% at week 8. Total Rx share now stands at 14.5%, capturing ground from Enhertu (down 3 points to 62%) and Kadcyla (Roche/Genentech, slipping to 18%). We're seeing particular strength in community oncology settings, where OncoLink-450's fixed-dose regimen—600 mg IV every 3 weeks—reduces treatment burden versus Enhertu's weight-based dosing, appealing to practices optimizing chair time amid ongoing labor shortages.

Regionally, U.S. performance accounts for 78% of sales, bolstered by J-code assignment in April, which streamlined reimbursement under Medicare Part B at our WAC of $14,500 per dose—strategically priced 12% below Enhertu's list to accelerate formulary wins. We've secured Tier 1 access on 68% of covered lives, including CVS Caremark and Express Scripts, with full P&T committee approvals pending Q3. In Europe, ex-U.S. sales contributed $42 million, primarily from Germany and the UK, where we've navigated HTA processes successfully; NICE in the UK recommended it as a Step 1 option, citing our cost-effectiveness at £11,200 per cycle versus Enhertu's £12,800. Japan launch is on track for H2, with a partnership with Eisai providing local infrastructure.

Key technical initiatives underpinning this momentum include our manufacturing scale-up at our Singapore facility, now at 120% capacity utilization, yielding a 92% yield on our novel linker-payload technology that minimizes off-target toxicity. We've also initiated a Phase IIIb label-expansion trial in gastric cancer, topline data expected Q4 2024, which could double our addressable market to $8 billion peak sales.

Shifting to HemaGene-12, our one-time gene therapy delivering functional Factor VIII expression via a high-capacity AAV8 capsid. Approved by FDA in Q4 last year for patients 18+ with severe hemophilia A without inhibitors, Q2 sales reached $112 million, up 180% QoQ, as we expanded into the inhibitor-eligible population via sBLA approval in May. This positions us directly against BioMarin's Roctavian and uniQure's etranacogene dezaparvovec, but with superior durability—our 2-year data shows 78% of patients achieving FVIII >15 IU/dL without bleeds, versus Roctavian's 62%.

Market share gains are equally compelling: Among new severe hemophilia A starts, we've captured 31% NRx share in the U.S., per Symphony Health, eroding Roctavian's dominance from 45% to 38%. Total treated patients now exceed 1,200, with annualized run-rate sales trajectorying toward $600 million by year-end. Pricing at $3.2 million per treatment—aligned with peers—has been supported by value-based agreements with payers like UnitedHealthcare, tying 20% of reimbursement to sustained bleed protection at 2 years.

Regionally, U.S. sales dominate at 92%, but we're making inroads in Europe with EMA approval and ASMF filings complete; initial uptake in Spain and Italy via compassionate use has converted to $18 million in Q2 revenue. Asia-Pacific remains a 2025 priority, with China NMPA submission leveraging our WuXi partnership for local fill/finish.

Strategically, these launches are turbocharging our overall revenue growth to 42% YoY, with new products contributing 65% of top-line. Trends we're monitoring include the biosimilar erosion wave—Imbruvica generics are pressuring the space, but our innovation moat in ADCs and gene therapies insulates us. Payer pushback on high-cost gene therapies is real, but our real-world evidence program, generating interim data on 500+ patients showing 85% reduction in ABR (annualized bleed rate), is de-risking that.

Looking forward, we guide Q3 OncoLink-450 sales to $400-450 million and HemaGene-12 to $150-175 million, with full-year new product revenue at $1.1-1.2 billion. Risks include supply chain constraints on platinum payloads, mitigated by dual-sourcing, and competitive readouts like AstraZeneca's Enhertu expansions. But with $2.8 billion in cash and a robust pipeline—including our bispecific T-cell engager in Phase II for AML—we're positioned to sustain 20%+ CAGR through 2027.

Now, turning to our marketing and sales effectiveness metrics for Q2, which continue to demonstrate robust execution across our portfolio, particularly for our flagship oncology asset, OncoTarget-X, and our recently launched immunology blockbuster, ImmunoBoost. As you know, in the pharma and biotech space, effectiveness isn't just about top-line revenue—it's about optimizing our $450 million annual sales and marketing budget to drive sustainable prescription growth, expand market share, and navigate a dynamic payer landscape reminiscent of the challenges seen with GLP-1 leaders like Novo Nordisk's Ozempic or Eli Lilly's Mounjaro.

Starting with the headline numbers: Total prescriptions—or TRx—across our core U.S. brands grew 18% year-over-year to 2.8 million scripts, with new-to-brand prescriptions, or NRx, up an impressive 24% to 1.1 million. This outpaced the broader oncology market, which per IQVIA data grew at just 12% YoY, allowing us to gain 2.2 share points in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) to 14.5% overall. In immunology, ImmunoBoost captured 8.7% market share in rheumatoid arthritis within nine months of launch, tracking ahead of AbbVie's Skyrizi trajectory at a similar stage.

Sales force productivity remains a cornerstone of our edge. Our 1,200-field-based representatives—optimized down from 1,400 last year through AI-driven territory realignments—delivered 22% higher scripts per rep at 2,350 per quarter, versus the industry average of 1,800 per Veeva CRM benchmarks. Reach and frequency metrics show we're hitting 92% of high-decile HCPs—those prescribers in the top 10% by volume—with an average of 7.2 details per HCP, up from 6.1 YoY. Conversion rates from detail to script improved to 14.5%, driven by our targeted messaging on OncoTarget-X's superior progression-free survival data from the Phase III Pinnacle trial.

On the marketing side, ROI has been stellar. Our omnichannel campaigns yielded a 4.2x return on ad spend (ROAS), with $120 million invested generating $504 million in attributable revenue—calculated via our proprietary Markov attribution model integrated with Komodo Health data. Digital channels were the star here: HCP engagement via our Veeva Engage platform surged 35% to 450,000 unique interactions, with email open rates at 42% and webinar attendance up 28% to 15,000 key opinion leaders (KOLs). Patient support programs, like our OncoTarget-X Co-Pay Navigator, boosted adherence by 16% to 78% at six months, directly lifting refill rates and extending treatment duration—a critical metric in oncology where we're seeing average therapy duration stretch to 11.2 months versus the category's 9.8.

Regionally, the U.S. remains our powerhouse, accounting for 72% of sales with 21% YoY prescription growth, fueled by expanded formulary access on CVS Caremark and Express Scripts lists—now covering 85% of commercial lives. In Europe, we're navigating pricing pressures post-IEHP reviews, but ex-U.S. prescriptions grew 14% to 650,000 TRx, with strong uptake in Germany and the UK for ImmunoBoost, where we've secured NICE reimbursement and gained 4.1 share points in the IL-17 inhibitor segment. Japan saw a 32% ramp-up for OncoTarget-X following PMDA approval, hitting 120,000 TRx as we leverage our partnership with Takeda for local detailing. Emerging markets like China contributed 6% of sales, with 15% growth via our Alibaba Health digital pilot, targeting tier-1 cities.

Strategically, we're leaning into technical initiatives to sustain this momentum. We've rolled out AI-powered next-best-action (NBA) recommendations in our Salesforce CRM, which increased close rates on KOL engagements by 19% by prioritizing HCPs based on predictive scripting models trained on 10 years of Symphony Health data. Our headless CMS for content personalization delivered a 27% lift in HCP time-on-site, mirroring Roche's digital playbook for Hemlibra. Looking ahead, we're allocating 25% more to non-personal promotion—up to $112 million in FY24—focusing on closed-loop marketing and real-world evidence (RWE) campaigns to counter biosimilar erosion risks, much like we're seeing with Humira's post-patent cliff.

In summary, these metrics underscore our disciplined approach: higher productivity, smarter spend, and deeper HCP-patient connections positioning us for 16-18% revenue growth in FY24.

I'll now turn to our outlook for the balance of the year and into 2025, along with the key catalysts that underpin our confidence in delivering sustained growth. As a reminder, our Q2 results came in ahead of consensus, with total revenue of $1.82 billion, up 18% year-over-year on a reported basis and 21% on a CER basis, driven primarily by 25% volume growth in our core oncology franchise, partially offset by an 8% headwind from US pricing pressures under the Inflation Reduction Act.

For the full year 2024, we are raising our revenue guidance to $7.45 billion to $7.60 billion, up from our prior range of $7.20 billion to $7.45 billion. This implies Q3 revenue of approximately $2.15 billion to $2.30 billion, representing sequential growth of 18% to 26% from Q2. Breaking it down by segment:

Net product sales are now expected to reach $6.95 billion to $7.05 billion, up 22% at the midpoint, led by our flagship PD-1 inhibitor, NeoVaxim-450 (neoVaxim), which we anticipate will deliver $4.85 billion in global sales, a 28% increase year-over-year. This reflects continued share gains in the frontline NSCLC setting, where neoVaxim's OS benefit over Keytruda has resonated with KOLs, pushing US TRx market share to 32% from 28% last quarter. Ex-US, we're guiding to 35% growth, fueled by reimbursement wins in Japan and expanded access in China via our partnership with Sinopharm.

Royalties and milestones of $500 million to $550 million, including a $150 million milestone from Roche upon topline data from their Phase 3 combo trial of neoVaxim plus their bispecific Tecentriq analog.

We continue to expect a modest contribution from our rare disease portfolio, with HemaGenix (our gene therapy for hemophilia B) ramping to $150 million in sales as US manufacturing scales post-BLA approval last quarter.

Regionally, US sales should comprise 65% of the total, growing 20% amid favorable payer mix shifts toward commercial lives, though tempered by IRA net pricing erosion of ~12%. Europe and rest-of-world will drive 25% growth, supported by EMA label expansions and tender wins in Brazil and Australia. China remains a high-conviction growth driver at 45% CAGR through 2025, albeit with near-term volatility from volume-based procurement.

Gross margins are guiding to 82% to 84% for the year, benefiting from manufacturing efficiencies at our Singapore facility and reduced COGS for our biosimilar InsuFlex (insulin glargine), now at 15% market penetration versus Sanofi's Lantus. OpEx as a percentage of revenue is expected to decline to 38% from 41%, reflecting disciplined R&D prioritization.

Looking ahead to 2025, we're initiating guidance for $8.75 billion to $9.00 billion in total revenue, implying 18% growth at the midpoint. This assumes neoVaxim achieves $5.75 billion, with upside from potential label expansions, and HemaGenix scaling to $450 million as community dosing centers come online.

Now, turning to our key upcoming catalysts, which we view as de-risking our trajectory and unlocking significant value inflection points:

First, Q1 2025 Phase 3 topline readout for neoVaxim in adjuvant melanoma (NCT04587891, n=1,200): Pivotal trial versus observation post-resection, powered for DFS. We modeled a 35% RFS improvement based on prior adjuvant data akin to Opdivo's readout. Positive data could expand the addressable market by $2.5 billion peak sales, with PDUFA in Q3 2025. This mirrors the transformative impact of Keytruda's melanoma approval in 2019, which added $3B+ annually.

Second, FDA PDUFA for HemaGenix next-gen vector (Q2 2025): Seeking approval for a lower-dose regimen reducing immunogenicity by 40%, based on our Pfizer-partnered AAV platform. Bridge data from our ongoing Phase 2 showed 95% FIX activity at 52 weeks, positioning it competitively against BioMarin's Roctavian, with superior durability.

Third, interim data from our CRISPR-based CAR-T for solid tumors (Q2 2025): CRISP-Tx1 in glioblastoma (n=45), with ORR endpoints. Early signals from the dose-escalation suggest 50%+ ORR, outpacing Novartis' Kymriah in neuro-oncology. This could validate our in vivo editing tech, similar to Beam Therapeutics' BEAM-101 progress.

Fourth, strategic partnership expansions: Finalizing terms for a $300 million upfront deal with Eli Lilly for our GLP-1/GLP-2 dual agonist in NASH, leveraging obesity market tailwinds post-Mounjaro's success. Additionally, European tender awards for InsuFlex expected by year-end, targeting 20% share in Germany and Italy.

Fifth, technical and operational catalysts: Completion of our Devens, MA fill-finish expansion in Q1, boosting capacity 50% for neoVaxim ahead of biosimilar entry in 2027. We're also advancing AI-driven patient matching via our PrecisionRx platform, which has improved trial enrollment 30% in our oncology studies, echoing Tempus' model.

These catalysts are sequenced to provide multiple shots on goal, with low execution risk given our 85% Phase 3 success rate historically. We remain committed to our capital allocation—$1.5 billion in share repurchases YTD, $2 billion dividend, and $3 billion pipeline investment—while maintaining a robust $8.2 billion cash position.

Next, let me provide a detailed breakdown of our product revenue performance by key drug franchises, with volume and price analysis. Overall, worldwide product revenues reached $2.85 billion in the quarter, up 18% year-over-year (YoY) on a reported basis and 19% at constant exchange rates (CER). This strong topline was driven by robust volume growth across our oncology and immunology franchises, partially offset by pricing headwinds from higher rebates in the U.S. and initial biosimilar erosion in Europe. Let me drill down franchise by franchise.

Oncology Franchise: $1.42 billion, +22% YoY reported (+23% CER)  
Our oncology portfolio, led by our PD-1/PD-L1 blockbuster OncoTarget-300 and the rapidly ramping BTK degrader Lynkora, continues to be our growth engine, representing 50% of total product revenues. OncoTarget-300 generated $1.15 billion, up 24% YoY, fueled by 16% volume expansion to 285,000 units sold worldwide—primarily from new patient starts in frontline NSCLC and expanding adoption in MSI-high endometrial cancer following our label expansion approval in Q2. U.S. volumes grew 19% to 180,000 units, supported by our KEYNOTE-like real-world evidence partnerships with NCCN centers, while ex-U.S. volumes rose 12%, with China contributing 25% of global OncoTarget volumes via our NRDL reimbursement since January. ASP held steady at $4,850 per unit globally, flat YoY despite a 3% U.S. rebate escalation to 48% gross-to-net (GTN) adjustments amid PBM negotiations—our value-based pricing contracts with payers like CVS Caremark mitigated further erosion.

Lynkora, our next-gen oral BTK for CLL and mantle cell lymphoma, delivered $275 million in its first full quarter post-launch, exceeding our guidance with 45,000 units sold. Pricing launched at a premium $7,200 ASP, 15% above Imbruvica equivalents, reflecting its best-in-class CROR profile from the Phase 3 LYNK-301 trial. Volumes were strongest in the U.S. (70% mix) and Japan, where we secured pricing parity with Chugai's Hemlibra in their HTA process.

Strategically, we're investing $150 million in our Singapore CMC hub to scale OncoTarget biosimilar-resistant next-gen bispecifics, targeting 25% market share gains versus Merck's Keytruda in 2025.

Immunology Franchise: $785 million, +12% YoY reported (+14% CER)  
Immunology revenues grew solidly to $785 million, driven by ImmuShield, our IL-17A/F inhibitor for moderate-to-severe psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis. ImmuShield posted $720 million, up 13% YoY, with volumes up 11% to 420,000 units amid steady TRx of 1.2 million and NRx share stable at 28% in the U.S. per IQVIA data—bolstered by our subcutaneous Q2W formulation switch, which improved patient adherence by 18% per our PRO data. U.S. volumes represented 55% of the total, growing 14% despite Stelara biosimilar launches from Alvotech and Amgen, which captured only 8% share to date thanks to our copay accumulator programs. ASP declined 1% YoY to $1,920 per unit globally, pressured by EU HTA clawbacks in Germany (down 4%) and U.S. 340B discounting expansion.

Our rare immunology asset, RARE-IMMU for primary immunodeficiency, added $65 million, up 25% YoY on 22% volume growth to 35,000 units, with emerging strength in Brazil via our local ANVISA filing. Looking ahead, we're advancing our TYK2 oral candidate from Phase 3 IMMU-405 into filing by year-end, positioning us to counter Tremfya's dominance.

Cardiovascular & Metabolics Franchise: $425 million, +8% YoY reported (+9% CER)  
CardioVasc, our PCSK9 siRNA for hypercholesterolemia, delivered $425 million, reflecting 10% volume growth to 210,000 units as we penetrate the statin-intolerant segment. U.S. growth was 12% (120,000 units), aided by our Outcomes2 trial data showing 65% LDL-C reduction versus Repatha, driving formulary wins with UnitedHealthcare. Ex-U.S., EU volumes rose 7% despite NICE pricing scrutiny, and we're on track for NRDL inclusion in China Q4. ASP dipped 2% YoY to $2,100 per unit from rebate inflation (U.S. GTN now 42%) and ROW tender pricing.

Metabolics, including our GLP-1/GIP agonist NovaSem for obesity, contributed $50 million in early launch revenues, with 15,000 units sold at $1,450 ASP—positioned competitively against Mounjaro but with superior GI tolerability from our Phase 3 data.

Rare Diseases & Other: $225 million, +15% YoY reported (+16% CER)  
Our GeneFix gene therapy for spinal muscular dystrophy (SMA) generated $180 million, up 18% YoY on 20% volume growth to 1,200 doses—U.S. demand remains robust post-Zolgensma competition, with patient starts up 22% via our newborn screening initiatives. ASP stable at $2.1 million per dose, supported by outcomes-based rebates tied to motor function milestones. Internationally, Japan approvals drove 30% ROW growth.

Other products, including legacy antivirals, added $45 million.

In aggregate, volumes drove 14% of our 18% YoY growth, with pricing contributing 4% after adjusting for a 300 bps GTN headwind. Regionally, U.S. was 62% of revenues (+20% YoY), Europe 22% (+12%), and ex-China emerging markets 16% (+25%). Technical initiatives like our viral vector scale-up at our North Carolina facility and AI-optimized supply chain reduced COGS by 5%, enabling reinvestment into 12 Phase 3 readouts next year.

For Q3, we guide to $2.9–3.0 billion in product revenues, with oncology accelerating to 25% growth. We're well-positioned amid biosimilar waves through our innovation moat—PD-1 combos, oral small molecules, and gene therapies—and disciplined pricing strategies.

Before closing out the prepared remarks, let me outline the key assumptions underpinning our projections for FY2025 and beyond, as well as the principal risk factors that could impact our performance. As always, these statements are forward-looking and subject to the safe harbor provisions outlined in our SEC filings. We'll be filing our 10-Q later this week with additional details.

Key Assumptions Driving FY2025 Guidance

Our FY2025 revenue guidance of $4.8 to $5.2 billion represents 18-25% year-over-year growth at the midpoint, building on the momentum from our core oncology franchise and the anticipated ramp-up of our next-generation pipeline. This assumes several foundational elements aligned with industry dynamics:

First, commercial execution and market share gains: We project VitaGle's (our PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody, approved by FDA in Q1 2024) U.S. net sales to reach $1.2 billion in FY2025, capturing 12-15% share in the frontline NSCLC market. This factors in a 92% gross-to-net adjustment, reflecting stable payer dynamics under the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), with ASPs holding at around $145,000 per patient-year. In Europe, EMA label expansion into hepatocellular carcinoma by mid-2025 supports €450 million in ex-U.S. sales, assuming reimbursement in key markets like Germany (AMNOG assessment at 85% of list price) and France (ASMR IV classification). Emerging markets, particularly China via our partnership with SinoBiopharm, contribute 10% of VitaGle royalties on $300 million in local sales, growing at 30% CAGR through patent exclusivity to 2038.

Second, pipeline milestones and probability-weighted success rates: Success in our late-stage assets is critical. For VG-301, our ADC targeting HER2-low breast cancer (similar to Enhertu), we assume 75% probability of positive Phase III topline in Q4 2025, enabling a 2026 launch with peak sales of $2.5 billion globally. This incorporates DAR 4.0 payload optimization and a 45% ORR from interim data. VG-402, a CRISPR-based gene editor for sickle cell disease (competing with Casgevy and Lyfgenia), assumes FDA accelerated approval in H2 2025 with 60% PwO success, pricing at $2.1 million per treatment course, akin to current standards, and U.S. uptake reaching 25,000 patients annually by 2028 amid NIH funding tailwinds.

Third, operational efficiencies and R&D productivity: We model SG&A at 22-24% of revenue, leveraging AI-driven patient services platforms (in partnership with Tempus) to boost adherence by 15%, reducing rebates. R&D expense grows 12% to $1.4 billion, focused on our "Precision Oncology 2.0" initiative—deploying single-cell RNA-seq and AlphaFold3 for target ID, yielding a 2.5x improvement in hit-to-lead rates versus historical benchmarks. Manufacturing assumes 95% on-time delivery from our Singapore facility, with CDMO yields at 88% for bispecifics, mitigating API shortages seen in 2023.

Fourth, macro and regional tailwinds: U.S. script growth of 8% in immuno-oncology, per IQVIA NPA data; EU tender wins at 70% bid success; and a 20% CAGR in China’s biosimilar-resistant segments. FX assumes USD/EUR at 1.08 and USD/CNY at 7.2. No material M&A is baked in, though we have $1.8 billion in dry powder for bolt-ons.

Principal Risk Factors and Sensitivities

While our base case is robust, we remain vigilant against headwinds inherent to biotech. Here's a breakdown of top risks, with quantified sensitivities where applicable:

First, clinical and regulatory risks (40% of Total Risk Weighting): Pipeline attrition remains binary. A VG-301 Phase III miss (25% base case risk) could defer $1.5 billion in NPV, pushing breakeven to 2029. Regulatory delays—e.g., FDA oncology review cycles averaging 10 months post-BLA—could shave 2-3 quarters off launches. We've stress-tested for a 20% pTsR haircut across our 12 Phase II/III programs, drawing from recent setbacks like Merck's Keytruda adjuvant failures.

Second, commercial and competitive pressures: Pricing erosion under IRA Part D redesign (effective 2025) caps max negotiation at 6 years post-launch for small molecules, potentially compressing VitaGle ASPs by 15-20% long-term. Biosimilar entry for our legacy TNF-alpha inhibitor (patent cliff 2026) risks $800 million revenue drop, offset partially by 40% gross margins on our biosimilar portfolio. Competition from Roche's Tirzepatide-like bispecifics or Bristol Myers' Opdivo expansions could limit NSCLC share to <10%, a 500 bps downside.

Third, reimbursement and access risks: In the U.S., 30% of Medicare Advantage plans tightening prior auths could slow VG-402 uptake by 20%. EU HTA harmonization under EHNR may yield 10-15% lower realized prices versus national assessments. Regional volatility—e.g., Brazil’s CMED price freezes or India’s compulsory licensing threats—caps EM growth at 15% downside.

Fourth, supply chain and geopolitical risks: API dependency on India/China (65% of spend) exposes us to tariffs or disruptions; a repeat of 2022 helium shortages for our CAR-T process could idle 15% capacity. Inflation at 3.5% (above our 2.5% assumption) lifts COGS by 200 bps.

Fifth, macroeconomic and legal risks: Recessionary pressure delaying trials (e.g., patient recruitment down 10-15%, per Tufts CSDD) or covenant breaches on our $2.5 billion term loan (2.2x net leverage target). IP challenges, like ongoing PTC litigation on VitaGle antibodies, carry 10% loss probability, eroding $500 million in royalties. Cybersecurity events, post-Change Healthcare, could disrupt 5% of rev rec.

In aggregate, our downside scenario—incorporating a 15% pipeline derate, 10% pricing haircut, and 5% FX weakening—yields FY2025 revenue of $4.2 billion, still +8% YoY. Upside levers include VG-301 label expansions (+$800 million) or strategic deals akin to Pfizer's Seagen acquisition.

We mitigate via diversified pipeline (oncology 55%, rare disease 30%, inflammation 15%), $3.2 billion cash runway (24 months at current burn), and robust insurance coverage. Our board-level risk committee reviews these quarterly, with enterprise risk management scoring at 4.2/5.0.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $480 million, or $1.32 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $550 million, or $1.50 per share. Our operating expenses were $900 million, reflecting continued investments in R&D to support our pipeline while maintaining discipline. Our cash position remains strong at $2.8 billion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Rachel Kim, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

**Dr. Rachel Kim, Chief Medical Officer:**
Thank you, Maria. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, our Phase IIIb label-expansion trial for OncoLink-450 in gastric cancer is advancing well, with topline data expected in Q4 2024. For HemaGene-12, real-world evidence continues to support its durability, with 78% of patients maintaining FVIII levels above 15 IU/dL at two years. In our oncology pipeline, the Phase 3 Pinnacle trial data for OncoTarget-X has driven strong adoption, and we're on track for the adjuvant melanoma readout for NeoVaxim-450 in Q1 2025. HemaGenix's next-gen vector PDUFA is slated for Q2 2025, showing promising 95% FIX activity. Additionally, interim data from CRISP-Tx1 in glioblastoma is encouraging, with early ORR over 50%. We expect to hit several upcoming milestones, including multiple Phase 3 readouts and regulatory submissions, de-risking our trajectory.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Michael.

**Dr. Michael Reynolds, CEO:**
Thank you, Rachel. We will now open the call for questions.

**Operator:**
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from John Ramirez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

**John Ramirez, Goldman Sachs:**
Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. On OncoLink-450, the uptake has been impressive. Can you expand on the payer access progress and how that factors into your Q3 guide for the product?

**Maria Gonzalez, CFO:**
Thanks, John. Great question. As I mentioned, we've secured Tier 1 access on 68% of covered lives, including CVS Caremark and Express Scripts, with P&T approvals pending Q3. The J-code and our 12% pricing discount versus Enhertu have accelerated formulary wins. This supports our Q3 guide of $400-450 million, assuming continued NRx share gains to 25% and ex-U.S. ramp in Germany and UK.

**Operator:**
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

**Lisa Chen, JPMorgan:**
Hi, team. On the marketing metrics, the sales force productivity and digital ROI stood out. How sustainable is the 4.2x ROAS, especially with biosimilar pressures?

**Dr. Michael Reynolds, CEO:**
Hi Lisa, thanks. Maria covered the details well—the AI-driven NBA tools and omnichannel focus have been key, with Veeva Engage interactions up 35%. This is sustainable as we shift 25% more to non-personal promo and RWE, countering erosion like Humira's cliff, while boosting adherence to 78%.
